newsitem.title: GREECE: Piraeus Bank H1 profit jumps 70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Piraeus Bank H1 profit jumps 70 pct.

text.p: Piraeus Bank said on Thursday its first half pretax profit rose 70 percent and should register growth of 56 percent this year, exceeding 5.0 billion drachmas ($18 million) versus 3.203 billion in 1996.
The bank's earnings forecast does not take into account proceeds from its ongoing 15.8 billion drachma rights issue which ends on Friday July 18.
The projected 1997 profit translates into earnings per share (EPS) of 520 drachmas based on an adjusted 11.5 million shares, it said.

The issue price for holders of rights is 2,500 drachmas, forming a price earnings ratio (P/E) of 4.8 and a price-to-book ratio (P/B) of around 1.0. Piraeus Bank's book value per share is 2,510 drachmas.
On a consolidated basis, pretax profit is expected to exceed 8.0 billion drachmas this year against 5.3 billion a year earlier.
Piraeus Bank shares gained 100 drachmas to settle at 4,430 on Thursday in moderate trade. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 277.2 Greek Drachmas)
